verdict: Good app, but not top-tier yet
verdict_explanation: A fresh critic pass on the drifted branch found one real structural issue: the bundled theme catalog was split across Redux state, persisted storage, and package-level constants even though only the selected theme ID is mutable. This loop removed that false ownership and now requires one more critic pass to re-score the branch from current source.

architecture_quality.proof: Pre-loop-3 theme ownership was split across packages/state/src/themeSlice.ts, packages/state/src/selectors.ts, apps/web/src/hooks/useTierDisplay.ts, and apps/web/src/pages/ThemesPage.tsx.

state_management.proof: Pre-loop-3 ThemeState stored both selectedThemeId and availableThemes even though reducers only wrote selectedThemeId.

domain_modeling.proof: packages/core/src/models.ts keeps Item.media?: ItemMedia, so impossible multi-URL state remains unrepresentable.
domain_modeling.residual_rationale_or_backlog_ref: Item.status remains a user-defined label rather than a closed enum.

data_flow.proof: packages/state/src/persistenceMiddleware.ts serialized the duplicated theme catalog and packages/state/src/store.ts restored it into runtime state.

framework_idioms.proof: Reducers remain pure, selectors are memoized, and the React/Redux integration stays idiomatic across the repo.
framework_idioms.residual_rationale_or_backlog_ref: The form cast stays inside a controlled input path.

concurrency.proof: No source-backed concurrency hazard is present; timeout cleanup and async ownership remain explicit.

simplicity.proof: The theme catalog traveled through state and persistence despite callers also using @tiercade/theme directly.

test_strategy.proof: The full contest gate passed after the refactor: core 109/109, state 64/64, ui 5/5, hooks 65/65.
test_strategy.residual_blocking_10: apps/web/e2e/ lacks a dedicated ItemMedia rendering path
test_strategy.residual_rationale_or_backlog_ref: Unit tests still cover the ItemMedia interface directly.

credibility.proof: Before this loop, Redux claimed ownership over bundled theme data that runtime readers still sourced directly from @tiercade/theme.

authority_map.owner: split between themeSlice.availableThemes, BUNDLED_THEMES, and findThemeById

strengths: headToHead.ts keeps real algorithmic depth behind a bounded interface.
createPersistenceMiddleware remains an injectable Storage seam with direct tests.
models.ts still encodes media as a discriminated union.
packages/core/test/dag.test.ts enforces the import DAG structurally.

findings.title: Bundled theme catalog is duplicated across Redux state and package constants
findings.why_it_matters: Static catalog data should have one authority; duplicating it across runtime state and package constants widens the state surface without leverage.
findings.what_is_wrong: Pre-loop-3 ThemeState stored availableThemes, persistence serialized it, and runtime readers still bypassed Redux through BUNDLED_THEMES and findThemeById.
evidence: packages/state/src/selectors.ts (pre-loop-3) exported selectAvailableThemes/selectCurrentTheme from Redux state
findings.leverage_impact: Callers had to learn which authority to trust for the same bundled catalog.
findings.locality_impact: Theme catalog changes spread through slice state, selectors, persistence, and UI readers.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Redux appeared to own bundled theme data that it did not actually control.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Keep only selectedThemeId in Redux, derive the bundled catalog from @tiercade/theme, and persist only the selected ID.

simplification_check.structurally_necessary: Removes false Redux ownership over bundled theme data and passes the deletion test for the extra slice field.
simplification_check.helpful_simplification: The state package now owns only the mutable choice: selectedThemeId.
simplification_check.should_not_be_done: Do not add a theme repository or another adapter layer.
simplification_check.tests_after_fix: Selector tests assert the bundled catalog/current theme interface directly; persistence test asserts only selectedThemeId is serialized.

backlog.title: Re-score after collapsing duplicated theme authority
backlog.why_it_matters: The refactor resolved the only fresh finding; the next critic pass determines whether the branch returns to contest-grade scores.
backlog.score_impact: architecture_quality + state_management + data_flow + simplicity + credibility back to 9.5

builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Reducers only mutate the selected ID, but the slice also carries the full bundled catalog.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Keep immutable bundled data in the package that defines it; keep only mutable choices in Redux.

builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Persisted JSON grows even though restore logic could recompute the data from code constants.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Persist only user choices and runtime state, not immutable bundled fixtures.

builder_notes.pattern: Public selector surface survives an internal simplification
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Callers need the same selector contract, but the authority behind it can move to a better source.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Preserve the interface; simplify the ownership behind it.

narrative: Loop 3 fixed the one drift-era structural deduction by collapsing the bundled theme catalog out of Redux state and persistence. The simplification helped: runtime ownership is now more honest, and a follow-up critic pass should be able to score the branch from current source without the old authority split.

loop_result.what_changed: Removed availableThemes from ThemeState, derived bundled themes through selectors, and tightened persistence/theme tests around selectedThemeId-only persistence.
loop_result.evidence_change_is_honest: Full contest gate passed: test:core 109/109, test:state 64/64, test:ui 5/5, test:hooks 65/65.

implementation_review.reason: All three checks passed; Redux now owns only the selected theme ID while the bundled catalog is derived from @tiercade/theme.
